verses.verse:
यदि प्रलम्बो बंशः स्याछिद्रं तत्र लघुस्मृतम्।
यदि वामनवद् बंशश्छिद्रं तत्र गुरुस्मृतम्।३६।
verses.text: If the bamboo is long, the hole there is held to be small; if the bamboo is short like a dwarf, the hole there is held to be large.

commentary.text: That is, if the bamboo is 10 times its paridhimāna (measure of the circumference), all the holes will be laghu (small). If it is seven times instead of ten, its holes will be large.

If this is not done, there is a chance of out-of-tuneness in Gāndhāra and Madhyama of the tāra saptaka (upper octave). In a bānsurī where both forms of Niṣāda depend on a single hole, that hole will have to be kept somewhat larger than the Dhaivata hole. And in a bānsurī where two holes are wanted for the two Niṣādas, both holes can be kept the same as Dhaivata's, or even a little smaller. So it is better to give all the holes a small form first, and afterwards make them bigger, matching them against a harmonium or some reliable instrument. For the solution to this fine point is audible, not visible.
